event: VXE 886 flew two fuel cells: fuel cell 508 over-temped and shut off in loiter (auto RTB), and on later flights both 508 and the second cell produced only about 408 to 417 W instead of 450 W, forcing an RTB.
component: SOFC heat exchanger chimney (flame extender) weld
failure_mode: weld between chimney and heat exchanger failed, chimney contacted the stack causing an internal short and temperature spike
contributing: resistance tack weld rather than laser weld on flame extender
possible vibration or warping of the bottom plate
second cell (998/988) showed early cell degradation of undetermined cause

evidence.quote: Fuel cell 508 shutoff in flight after saying it was over temp, next flight failed to produce 450 watts in flight
Once we launched and established in our loiter were only generating 408 watts I believe, and constantly in a 1w deficit for the entire flight
Molten silver present on the chimney confirms contact here causing the short and conversely the temperature spike causing the fault.
This particular weld failure has been an observed and recorded finding previously in AA.

team_root_cause: 508 suffered a sudden internal short. The weld between the chimney and heat exchanger failed, either from vibration on a poor weld or warping of the bottom plate severing the weld. Molten silver present on the chimney confirms contact here causing the short and conversely the temperature spike causing the fault. Evidence is also present on the end zal with damage caused during removal due to flame extender not being parallel to the stack.

would_settle_it.what: teardown photo of the failed chimney weld and molten silver on fuel cell 508

would_settle_it.file: Ann Arbor teardown record for the second fuel cell
would_settle_it.what: why cell degradation appeared after so few cycles on the second stack

reasoning: Fuel cell 508 over-temped and shut off in flight. The Ann Arbor teardown found the chimney to heat exchanger weld had failed and molten silver on the chimney, showing contact and an internal short that explains the temperature spike. The team traced it to the tack weld process and changed to laser welding.
notes: Two fuel cells on one ticket. The second cell is written as both 998 and 988; its low output was put down to early cell degradation with cause not determined. RMA-1059 attachment is a blank RMA form.

event: On VXE 966 the abort button on the Razor (and Xbox) hand controller did not abort the landing back to IP1; only pause worked, and on another attempt a held pause did not take until selected in the OGCS VTOL window.
failure_mode: joystick abort to IP1 while enroute to or in the landing pattern was never implemented in OGCS or Jennings; abort only allowed after IP5
contributing: miscommunication about feature availability to operators and instructors

evidence.quote: VXE 966 - Abort button on the Razor hand controllers to not function to abort the landing and return to IP1 of the landing plan.
ticket updated - this feature was never implemented in OGCS or Jennings and was likely expected to work based on a miscommunication.
OGCS does not allow aborting from the joystick until after IP5, at which point the abort window is extremely small. Realistically, only pause can be executed from the joystick.
Fix implemented and merged.

team_root_cause:
The root cause is a miscommunication about this features availability.  This behavior was never implemented in Jennings or OGCS.
The abort button on all joysticks (XBOX, Razor, SCIP, etc.) does not allow aborts while enroute to or in the landing pattern.
OGCS does not allow aborting from the joystick until after IP5, at which point the abort window is extremely small. Realistically, only pause can be executed from the joystick.
reasoning: Software engineering confirmed the joystick abort to IP1 was never implemented, so the button behaved as coded. The fix was added in OGCS 1.5.0 under OGCS-617.
notes: The second report (Xbox controller pause held from 150 ft to 40 ft not taking effect) is not explained by the root cause and was not addressed separately. The attached form has no event statements filled in.

event: On VXE 880 the operator switched AUX 1 payload power off in flight to deal with gimbal issues, the MCM reset, the mission plan was lost and new missions could not be uploaded, but the aircraft was landed safely with Loiter Here Now and Land PLZ.
component: MCM power supply path on non-critical payload bus (SLA Breakout Board / TPS16630 eFuse)
failure_mode: payload power cycle transient (inrush or ground shift) reset the MCM, restarting VSM/OGCS and dropping the mission and reference altitude
contributing: operator power cycled AUX 1 (E95 gimbal) in flight
VSM restart in flight not a supported contingency
Avionics box revision for 880 not stated

evidence.quote: In this case, it was a full power cycle and reboot of the MCM, in which all services (namely OGCS/VSM) were started automatically.
added screen recording and logs from bench testing recreating issue just by cycling gimbal power
- Resulting back-fed inrushcurrent tripping the fast-tripcomparator on the TPS16630Efuse (max 45A)
- Risk exists when powering on 28V payloads. The payload power return is common with the MCM on certain avionics boxes.

team_view_in_comments: In this case, it was a full power cycle and reboot of the MCM, in which all services (namely OGCS/VSM) were started automatically.

would_settle_it.what: command log timing of AUX 1 off (and any on) against the MCM reset

would_settle_it.file: VXE 880 avionics box part number and revision
would_settle_it.what: whether 880 has Avbox V4 Rev G or earlier (SLA Breakout V2, MCM on non-critical bus)

reasoning: Engineering confirmed a full MCM power cycle followed the AUX 1 off command, and the reporter reproduced it on the bench by cycling gimbal power. VXEP-1315 documents MCM resets from payload power transients on the shared non-critical bus tripping the TPS16630 eFuse. The VXEP-1315 team itself notes an AUX 1 off reset was surprising and 880's avbox revision is not given, so this is narrowed to the MCM payload power path, not one confirmed part.
notes: Root Cause field holds only a link to VXEP-1315. The front-end log only shows GCS window closes and STANAG config validation errors, no MCM detail.

event: VXE 557 (SOCOM) on landing took pause but seemed not to nudge, the lift motors pulsed audibly from about 20 ft, the aircraft dropped and kept pulsing after touchdown; aircraft intact.
failure_mode: significant cell imbalance and voltage drop in the HLB during the VTOL landing
contributing: GCS pause flood: 10 second pause reissued about every 300 ms
nudge inputs were small but were acted on by the autopilot

evidence.quote: HLB seems to really drop during landing could this cause the nudge issues?
That HLB cell drop would cause critical control issues.
It appears that the autopilot is responding to the commands (note the position command and feedback slewing per the override inputs).
It appears that nudging was working although the inputs were minor and that extensive pausing occurred, but I think significant imbalance on the cells was occurring prior to the pausing.

team_view_in_comments: I think significant imbalance on the cells was occurring prior to the pausing.

would_settle_it.what: HLB cell voltages during landing, size and timing of the drop
HLB tester run to find the weak cell (battery is overseas and not expected back)

reasoning: Log review showed nudge commands did reach and move the autopilot, so the missed nudge was really small inputs under a continuous pause flood. The HLB showed a large cell drop and imbalance that started before the pausing, which engineers say would cause the control problems seen. The battery was not returned, so no specific cell or cause inside the HLB is known.
notes: Label HLB_bad_cell. Executive summary gives probable cause battery issue.
